newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil premiums firm $1 on good demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil premiums firm $1 on good demand.

text.p: NWE heating oil premiums were around $1 firmer on Friday, helped by strong French and German demand and scarce January vessels, traders said.
Heating oil was firmly supported despite a 6-10 day forecast of normal temperatures, trading $1 firmer at Feb +$10 cif NWE, and was later bid into France at Feb IPE +$10.
Russian was done unchanged at Feb +$7.75 cif NWE. German winter grade heating oil was assessed steady at Feb IPE +$9/10. A low sulphur diesel cargo traded $2 lower at Feb IPE +$15 cif NWE.
Asian and U.S. arbs were closed.
Benchmark February gas oil futures closed down $3 at $215.75 a tonne, tracking crude lower. A sharp mid-session fall prompted cautious sentiment in physicals, traders said.

Barge premiums were stable at Feb IPE +$9 traded for German quality and storage was around Feb IPE +6/7 in dull trade. Heating oil for the second half of Febuary traded at Feb +$1. Low sulphur was around $1 firmer at Feb IPE +$12/14.

Volume was depressed by buyer reluctance amid hopes of lower prices and forecasts of normal temperatures. But demand was supported by news of below normal German domestic heating fuel stocks at the end of December.
